_about: World Domination, the last act of the grand campaign. The war between the alliances is decided when a great power has fallen and no two great powers still standing are at war with each other. From then on the player may take the victory, or choose World Domination: every alliance is dissolved, every nation still standing is at war with every other, and the last one standing has won. Choosing it cannot be undone. A historical scenario has none of this, and neither has a war with nobody at the table.

nerve._about: With every neighbour an enemy, a computer-run staff opens an offensive at this share of the odds it would want in an ordinary war (attackAt), and keeps one going at this share (persist).

guests._about: Troops standing on a former ally's soil when the alliances are dissolved go home under safe conduct: to the nearest ground their own nation holds, or to its capital by sea. They arrive with this much of their organisation and cannot move again that month.

lines._about: What the news says as the last act opens, by who chose it. {n} is the number of nations still standing.
lines.open: World Domination. Every alliance is dissolved and every treaty is paper. {n} nations are left, each alone and at war with all the rest. The last one standing takes the world.
lines.guests: Armies on a former ally's soil are given safe conduct home: {n} corps cross the old frontiers for the last time.
lines.leave: {name} takes its armies and fleets home across the ocean and shuts its ports to the Old World.
lines.won: {name} stands alone. There is nobody left to fight: the world is {adj}.
